notes: Plain definitions shown as tips wherever the word appears. Terms marked "from": "brief" are Tom's own definitions (Light Lab brief, section 2). Terms written for the app were approved by Tom on Nov 17 2026.

key light.def: The main light. The brightest. Sets the direction of the shadows.

fill light.def: A softer light that lightens the shadows the key makes.

back light.def: A light behind the subject that outlines the head and shoulders.

hair light.def: A back light aimed at the top of the head (optional extra).

high-key.def: Bright, even, few shadows. Fill nearly matches the key. Usually a bright backdrop.

low-key.def: Dark and dramatic. Deep shadows. Little or no fill.

modifier.def: A tool that shapes light (softbox, umbrella, beauty dish, snoot or grid, barn doors).

soft light.def: Big, close light gives soft shadows. Small, far light gives hard shadows.

falloff.def: Light gets weaker as it moves farther from the subject.

color temperature.def: How warm (orange) or cool (blue) a light is.

three-point.def: The classic setup: a key light, a fill light and a back light.

softbox.def: A fabric box over a light that makes it bigger and softer.

umbrella.def: Light shot through or bounced off an umbrella: a big, soft source.

snoot.def: A tube on a light that makes a small, tight spot.

gel.def: A sheet of coloured plastic in front of a light that changes its colour.

gobo.def: A metal cut-out in front of a light that projects a pattern, like a window or blinds.

barn doors.def: Metal flaps on a light that fold in to cut light off one side of the beam.

flag.def: A black card that blocks light from where you don't want it.

reflector.def: A white, silver or gold card that bounces light back onto the subject.

feathering.def: Turning a light so only the soft edge of its beam reaches the subject.

lighting ratio.def: How much brighter the lit side is than the shadow side. 2:1 is soft; 8:1 is dramatic.

stop.def: One stop is double (or half) the light. 2 stops = 4 times, 3 stops = 8 times.

aperture.def: How wide the lens opens. A small f-number (f/1.8) lets in more light and blurs the backdrop more.

shutter speed.def: How long the camera takes in light. Longer (1/30) is brighter than shorter (1/500).

ISO.def: How sensitive the camera is. Higher ISO is brighter but adds grain.

white balance.def: What the camera treats as white. Lights warmer than it look orange; cooler ones look blue.

depth of field.def: How much of the picture is sharp from front to back. Wide apertures make it shallow, so the backdrop blurs.

exposure.def: How bright the camera makes the picture, set by aperture, shutter speed and ISO.
